articles.title: MP’s ‘Bittu Tabahi’ joins Bengaluru forest cleanup drive with environmentalist AN Yellappa Reddy
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Surendra Singh Choudhary, the 21-year-old Madhya Pradesh environmentalist known as ‘Bittu Tabahi’ for his solo cleanup of the heavily pollu.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Surendra Singh Choudhary, the 21-year-old Madhya Pradesh environmentalist known as ‘Bittu Tabahi’ for his solo cleanup of the heavily polluted Ajnar River, joined a cleanliness drive at Turahalli Forest near BSK 6th Stage in Bengaluru on Saturday.Choudhary took part in the drive along with local residents, civic organisations and active citizen collectives.The initiative was carried out in collaboration with local lifestyle brand Ecological Drive and also saw the participation of Indian environmentalist and retired Indian Forest Service officer AN Yellappa Reddy.Choudhary, who gained attention after documenting his efforts to clean the Ajnar River in Biaora, Rajgarh district, has since expanded his environmental work beyond his hometown.He began cleaning the plastic-choked Ajnar River on January 26, spending around Rs 30,000 of his own money on basic tools and supplies.He cleaned three major ghats despite having no proper protective gear or even knowing how to swim.His efforts later drew attention from industrialist Anand Mahindra and Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav.Former England cricketer Kevin Pietersen also praised the cleanup as “heroic” and said it deserved international recognition.The campaign eventually led to Boyan Slat, founder and CEO of Netherlands-based environmental organisation The Ocean Cleanup, offering Choudhary a job.Choudhary later told TOI that Slat had contacted him and taken down his credentials, though the exact role had not yet been discussed.The Ajnar cleanup also prompted the Biaora municipal corporation to deploy JCB and Poclain machines to remove accumulated waste and polythene from the river.Choudhary has since said his objective is not limited to the Ajnar and that he articles.title: Entre a fé e o crime: investigação revela vida dupla de missionária | G1
articles.standfirst: Mensagens, fotos e vídeos obtidos pela polícia indicam proximidade de família de religiosos com integrantes do crime organizado em Mato Grosso.
articles.summary: Mensagens, fotos e vídeos obtidos pela polícia indicam proximidade de família de religiosos com integrantes do crime organizado em Mato Grosso.
articles.body:
Uma investigação da Polícia Civil de Mato Grosso revelou a suposta atuação de uma família de missionários religiosos em um esquema ligado ao Comando Vermelho. Segundo os investigadores, Rhavenna Barcelos de Almeida e seus pais, os pastores Nivaldo de Almeida e Orminda de Almeida, usavam o acesso a presídios para manter contato com integrantes da facção, movimentar recursos financeiros e fortalecer vínculos com criminosos.

De acordo com a Delegacia de Repressão ao Crime Organizado (Draco), a família fazia parte de um grupo autorizado pelo governo de Mato Grosso a prestar assistência religiosa em unidades prisionais. A investigação começou após uma denúncia que apontava a ligação dos três com membros da organização criminosa.

Investigação revelou a suposta atuação de uma família de missionários religiosos em um esquema ligado ao crime organizado — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Os investigadores afirmam que os suspeitos se aproveitaram da atividade religiosa para se aproximar de lideranças do crime organizado que cumpriam pena na Penitenciária Central do Estado, em Cuiabá. Segundo a polícia, eles transmitiam recados, emprestavam contas bancárias para movimentação de dinheiro e ajudavam a ocultar recursos provenientes do tráfico de drogas.

Materiais obtidos durante a investigação, com autorização judicial, incluem mensagens, fotos, vídeos e áudios que, segundo a polícia, demonstram a proximidade de Rhavenna Barcelos de Almeida com integrantes da facção. Entre os registros analisados, há imagens da investigada exibindo armas, grandes quantias em dinheiro, joias e veículos de luxo.

Missionária usava acesso a presídios para se relacionar com criminosos e ajudar crime organizado, diz investigaçã — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Um dos principais nomes citados no inquérito é Jonas Souza Gonçalves Júnior, conhecido como Batman. Apontado pela polícia como uma das lideranças do Comando Vermelho em Mato Grosso, ele cumpria pena na mesma unidade prisional frequentada pela família durante as atividades religiosas.

Segundo a investigação, Batman recebeu autorização para cumprir pena em regime semiaberto em setembro de 2024, mas rompeu a tornozeleira eletrônica poucos dias depois e fugiu para o Rio de Janeiro. A polícia afirma que Rhavenna Barcelos de Almeida mantinha contato frequente com o criminoso e sabia exatamente onde ele estava escondido. Mensagens analisadas pelos investigadores mostram o compartilhamento de localização e diálogos sobre operações policiais realizadas no Complexo do Alemão.

A investigação também concluiu que os dois tinham um relacionamento amoroso. De acordo com a polícia, a missionária viajava com frequência ao Rio de Janeiro, onde se encontrava com o traficante e participava de momentos de lazer financiados pelo grupo criminoso.

Missionária suspeita de envolvimento com crime organizado mantinha relacionamento com criminosos, diz polícia — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Os investigadores apontam que a rotina de Rhavenna Barcelos de Almeida era marcada pela ostentação. Entre os materiais apreendidos estão registros em carros de luxo, joias, festas e viagens. A polícia afirma que um Porsche avaliado em cerca de R$ 600 mil, exibido pela investigada nas redes sociais, pertencia a Batman.

Além dela, outras mulheres que frequentavam os presídios como missionárias também passaram a ser investigadas. Segundo a Draco, algumas mantinham relacionamentos com traficantes e teriam mentido em depoimentos prestados à polícia, motivo pelo qual foram indiciadas por falso testemunho.

Investigação revela envolvimento de missionária com o crime organizado — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Segundo relacionamento com liderança da facção

A polícia também identificou uma ligação de Rhavenna Barcelos de Almeida com Renildo Silva Rios, apontado como um dos fundadores do Comando Vermelho em Mato Grosso e preso há mais de duas décadas por crimes como homicídio, tráfico e organização criminosa.

De acordo com o inquérito, os dois mantinham um relacionamento amoroso. A investigação aponta que o preso enviava presentes à investigada, incluindo joias e um veículo. Conversas obtidas pela polícia mostram que ela tinha conhecimento da posição de destaque ocupada por Renildo dentro da facção.

Rhavenna Barcelos de Almeida, Orminda de Almeida e Nivaldo de Almeida foram indiciados por organização criminosa e lavagem de dinheiro. Posteriormente, o Ministério Público denunciou Rhavenna, Orminda e Renildo pelos mesmos crimes.

A Justiça de Mato Grosso proibiu os investigados e outras quatro pessoas citadas no inquérito de participarem de atividades de assistência religiosa em unidades prisionais. A Secretaria de Justiça informou que reforçou a fiscalização contra o uso de celulares dentro da Penitenciária Central de Cuiabá.

Em nota, a defesa de Rhavenna Barcelos de Almeida negou as acusações e afirmou que os fatos serão esclarecidos durante o processo. Já a defesa de Orminda de Almeida declarou que a investigada não tem qualquer participação em organização criminosa.

Investigação revela suposta vida dupla de missionária — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Nesta semana, Nivaldo de Almeida morreu em consequência de um câncer.

articles.title: Jovem expulso por ser gay ganha R$ 100 mil de indenização dos pais | G1
articles.standfirst: Emanuel Roque relata ameaças, abandono afetivo e rejeição à orientação sexual; caso aconteceu em Santa Catarina.
articles.summary: Emmanuel relata ameaças, abandono afetivo e rejeição à orientação sexual; caso aconteceu em Santa Catarina.
articles.body:
A Justiça de Santa Catarina condenou um casal a pagar R$ 100 mil de indenização ao próprio filho por danos morais, violência e abandono afetivo. A decisão envolve o caso de Emanuel Roque, jovem que afirma ter sido ameaçado, hostilizado e expulso de casa pelos pais após assumir um relacionamento homoafetivo.

Morador de Jaguaruna, no Sul catarinense, Emanuel trabalhava com o pai em uma loja da família e tinha 17 anos quando começou a namorar Jonathas, colega de escola que também trabalhava em um mercado da cidade. Segundo ele, o relacionamento marcou um momento importante de autoconhecimento.

"Foi a primeira vez que eu me aceitei", relatou o jovem. "Parece que saiu um peso das minhas costas."

De acordo com Emanuel, os pais não aceitaram a relação. Ele afirma que foi pressionado a deixar o emprego e impedido de continuar frequentando a escola. O jovem também relata ter sido alvo de ofensas após revelar à mãe que estava namorando.

"Ela começou a gritar no meio da sala, falando que tinha nojo de mim", afirmou.

Justiça condena pais a pagarem indenização de R$ 100 mil a filho expulso de casa — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Segundo o relato apresentado no processo, as agressões evoluíram para ameaças físicas. Emanuel afirma que o pai o intimidou com um alicate durante uma discussão.

"Eu fiquei com medo. Botei a mão na mão dele e ele me jogou no chão", disse.

O jovem também relatou um episódio envolvendo uma arma de fogo.

"Botou na minha cabeça e falou que ia me meter um balaço", afirmou.

Ainda conforme o processo, o pai teria feito publicações com conteúdo homofóbico nas redes sociais e ameaçado Jonathas pela internet. O caso chegou ao Conselho Tutelar após uma denúncia feita por um amigo de Emanuel.

Jovem expulso de casa por ser gay consegue indenização na Justiça contra os pais — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Os pais admitiram não aceitar a orientação sexual do filho e, segundo registros do caso, afirmaram que ele teria de deixar a residência caso mantivesse o relacionamento. Pouco tempo depois, Emanuel foi acolhido em um abrigo municipal, onde permaneceu por quase um ano.

Ele descreve o período como um momento de reconstrução.

"No começo, realmente, foi muito difícil", afirmou. "Mas as pessoas que estavam lá eu posso chamar de família".

Ao falar sobre o acolhimento recebido, o jovem foi ainda mais enfático:

"Foi o lugar que eu fui mais acolhido na minha vida."

Em outro momento, definiu o abrigo como o local onde finalmente encontrou segurança.

O Ministério Público de Santa Catarina acompanhou o caso e ingressou com ação por abandono afetivo e violação de direitos. A investigação reuniu provas como publicações em redes sociais, registros de mensagens e depoimentos de testemunhas.

A sentença determinou o pagamento de R$ 100 mil por danos morais, com correção monetária e juros. Os pais também foram proibidos de realizar publicações relacionadas ao filho nas redes sociais.

Ao comentar a decisão judicial, Emanuel afirmou:

"Meu pai sempre fez tudo achando que não ia ter consequência, mas tem."

Os pais de Emanuel, Iremar Roque e Terezinha Aparecida da Silva Roque, negam as acusações e ainda podem recorrer da decisão. A reportagem também tentou contato com o casal e os advogados, mas não obteve retorno.

Hoje morando no Rio Grande do Sul com Jonathas, o jovem afirma que ainda espera recuperar a relação com a família.

"Eu sei que um dos princípios de Jesus, de Deus, é o perdão. No momento em que eles me pedirem perdão e eu perdoar, e a gente voltar a ser uma família, tudo vai ficar bem. Eles sempre vão ser os meus pais".

articles.title: 'Salvo pelo gongo': Alex Escobar relata diagnóstico de doença rara | G1
articles.standfirst: Em entrevista, jornalista relata os momentos de incerteza até o diagnóstico e fala sobre a adaptação à nova rotina.
articles.summary: Em entrevista, jornalista relata os momentos de incerteza até o diagnóstico e fala sobre a adaptação à nova rotina.
articles.body:
O jornalista Alex Escobar descobriu que tem miastenia gravis , uma doença autoimune rara, depois de apresentar dificuldade para falar durante uma transmissão ao vivo na cobertura da Copa do Mundo, em Nova Jersey, nos Estados Unidos. Os exames também identificaram um tumor no timo, glândula localizada no peito. A orientação médica foi retirar o tumor por meio de uma cirurgia.

Antes do episódio, Escobar já sentia dificuldades para mastigar. Segundo o jornalista, os sintomas começaram cerca de dois meses antes da viagem para a Copa. Ele começava a comer normalmente, mas, ao longo da refeição, passava a apresentar uma limitação para abrir a boca.

No dia da transmissão, a dificuldade voltou durante o café da manhã. Mesmo assim, Escobar se posicionou para participar ao vivo do SportTV News. Quando começou a falar, percebeu que não conseguia pronunciar algumas palavras.

“Minha língua estava dura, que é um sintoma da doença, da miastenia”, relatou.

Durante a entrada, o jornalista repetiu a frase “Neymar treinou” na tentativa de conseguir falar corretamente e concluir a participação. Ele explicou que estava consciente durante todo o episódio e que a repetição das palavras não foi provocada por confusão mental, como alguns internautas chegaram a especular na internet.

“Eu estava completamente consciente do que estava acontecendo”, afirmou.

Veja a entrevista completa no vídeo acima.

Alex Escobar fala sobre retorno ao trabalho depois do diagnóstico de Miastenia Gravis — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Após deixar a transmissão, Escobar foi levado a um hospital e permaneceu internado por dois dias. Os exames descartaram um acidente vascular cerebral, o AVC. Nos Estados Unidos, os médicos levantaram a possibilidade de esclerose múltipla.

O jornalista enviou os resultados ao médico Emanuel, no Brasil. Segundo Escobar, o clínico descartou a suspeita de esclerose múltipla, mas identificou uma massa no mediastino, região localizada no centro do tórax.

Sem um diagnóstico conclusivo, Escobar retornou sozinho ao Brasil. Ele classificou a viagem como o momento mais difícil do processo.

“Eu peguei um avião sozinho, voltando para casa e no escuro. Eu não tinha a menor ideia do que eu tinha. Podia ser tudo”, contou.

No Rio de Janeiro, o jornalista foi encaminhado ao neurologista Felipe Schmidt, professor da Universidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro, a Uerj. Após avaliar o caso, o médico indicou a suspeita de miastenia gravis.

A miastenia gravis é uma doença autoimune. Isso significa que o sistema de defesa do organismo passa a atacar, por engano, a comunicação entre os nervos e os músculos. Os anticorpos impedem essa ligação, o que provoca fraqueza muscular.

Os primeiros sinais podem ser sutis. Entre os sintomas estão pálpebra caída, visão dupla e dificuldades para mastigar, falar, engolir ou segurar objetos. O esforço pode agravar o cansaço, enquanto uma pausa de alguns minutos pode aliviar os sintomas.

De acordo com especialistas, a doença, na maioria das vezes, não tem cura. No entanto, o tratamento pode controlar o quadro, levar à remissão ou reduzir os sintomas, permitindo que o paciente tenha uma vida normal ou próxima do normal.

Em parte dos casos, a miastenia gravis pode estar relacionada a uma alteração no timo. A glândula fica no meio do peito, atrás do osso esterno, e desempenha um papel importante na infância, quando ajuda no amadurecimento das células de defesa. Na vida adulta, perde função.

Alterações nessa glândula, como um tumor, podem fazer o organismo produzir células que atacam os músculos por engano. No caso de Escobar, os exames identificaram um tumor no timo, e os médicos decidiram retirá-lo por meio de uma cirurgia.

Ao comentar o diagnóstico, o jornalista disse que passou a encarar as dificuldades provocadas pela doença com gratidão, porque a investigação permitiu descobrir o tumor.

“Eu fui salvo pelo gongo. O gongo se chama miastenia. Então, tudo que eu tenho passado de perrengue, eu passo agradecendo”, afirmou.

Escobar também relatou uma conversa com o neurologista sobre os riscos que correria caso o tumor não tivesse sido diagnosticado.

“O doutor Felipe, neurologista, falou: ‘Você tinha, acho, mais um ano de vida. Poderia morrer de infarto sem saber que tinha um tumor’”, contou.

O jornalista afirmou que pretende retomar o trabalho de forma gradual. A primeira etapa será a gravação de textos em off, sem aparecer diante das câmeras. Depois, ele deverá gravar programas-piloto para avaliar como o organismo reage à rotina.

Segundo Escobar, o ajuste dos medicamentos ainda não eliminou completamente os sintomas. Por isso, uma nova dificuldade de fala ainda pode ocorrer durante as transmissões.

“Os médicos dizem que a gente vai chegar num momento em que vai haver um ajuste de medicamento em que eu não vou ter mais sintoma. Esse momento não chegou totalmente ainda”, afirmou.

O jornalista pediu compreensão do público caso volte a apresentar alguma limitação diante das câmeras. Ele explicou que, se isso acontecer, pretende continuar a transmissão e aguardar até que a fala volte ao normal.

“Eu só vou precisar de 30 segundinhos para que tudo volte ao normal. Então, não se assustem”, disse.

articles.title: Defesa Civil de Rio das Ostras alerta para chuva e ventos fortes | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o órgão, frente fria deve provocar pancadas de chuva, com acumulado de até 50 milímetros em um dia; Inmet prevê rajadas acima de 40 km/h.
articles.summary: Segundo o órgão, frente fria deve provocar pancadas de chuva, com acumulado de até 50 milímetros em um dia; Inmet prevê rajadas acima de 40 km/h.
articles.body:
Defesa Civil aberta para chuva e ventos fortes na segunda e terça — Foto: Pexels

A Defesa Civil de Rio das Ostras (RJ) emitiu um alerta na tarde deste domingo (13) para a possibilidade de chuva forte e ventos intensos entre o fim da manhã de segunda-feira (14) e a manhã de terça-feira (15).

Segundo o órgão, a aproximação e passagem de uma frente fria, seguida pelo transporte de umidade do oceano para o continente, podem provocar pancadas de chuva de intensidade moderada a forte, com altos acumulados, além de rajadas de vento.

De acordo com o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet), são esperados acumulados de chuva entre 20 e 30 milímetros por hora, podendo chegar a 50 milímetros em um dia. Os ventos podem ultrapassar 40 km/h.

A Defesa Civil recomenda que moradores fiquem atentos às condições climáticas e evitem áreas de risco durante o período.

Em caso de emergência, a população pode ligar para o 199 ou entrar em contato com a Defesa Civil pelo WhatsApp: (22) 2760-8394.

Feche portas, janelas e cortinas para reduzir o risco de danos provocados pelo vento

Evite deixar objetos em locais altos ou que possam ser deslocados pelo vento

Em caso de falta de energia elétrica, prefira o uso de lanternas. Evite utilizar velas devido ao risco de incêndio

Não permaneça em piscinas, rios, lagos ou outras áreas próximas à água durante as tempestades

Evite áreas alagadas e não atravesse ruas com correnteza

Não se abrigue sob árvores, estruturas metálicas ou em locais próximos a postes

Evite atividades e esportes ao ar livre durante a ocorrência de raios e ventos fortes

Evite permanecer ou estacionar veículos próximos a árvores, placas, torres e outras estruturas que possam ser derrubadas pelo vento

Fique atento a fios elétricos rompidos e à possibilidade de queda de galhos e árvores

articles.title: Em meio à tensão comercial com os EUA, premiê do Canadá diz buscar 'aliança única' com a União Europeia | G1
articles.standfirst: UE e Ottawa discutem facilitar a circulação de trabalhadores e ampliar a integração em setores estratégicos, como energia, defesa e inteligência artificial, segundo o Wall Street Journal.
articles.summary: UE e Ottawa discutem facilitar a circulação de trabalhadores e ampliar a integração em setores estratégicos, como energia, defesa e IA, segundo o Wall Street Journal.
articles.body:
FILE PHOTO: Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney suspends trade negotiations with the U.S. — Foto: Chris Tanouye

O primeiro-ministro do Canadá, Mark Carney , afirmou neste domingo (13) que o país quer construir uma "aliança única" com a União Europeia (UE), mas sem se tornar membro do bloco.

A declaração foi dada após o jornal Wall Street Journal informar que Ottawa estaria avaliando uma possível associação formal com a UE.

Segundo o jornal, o bloco europeu estaria aberto a conceder ao Canadá uma categoria inédita de membro associado. O status ainda precisaria ser criado e representaria uma exceção para um bloco que historicamente adota regras rígidas para a entrada de novos integrantes.

“Não estamos buscando nos tornar membros da União Europeia”, afirmou Carney. “O que estamos buscando, e para o que vamos iniciar discussões, é uma aliança única entre o Canadá e a União Europeia”, disse a jornalistas durante o Festival Internacional de Cinema de Toronto.

“Compartilhamos os mesmos valores, temos as mesmas prioridades e forças muito complementares", acrescentou. A aproximação ocorre em meio ao agravamento das tensões comerciais entre o Canadá e os EUA .

O gabinete de Carney confirmou no sábado (12) que ele viajará à França e ao Reino Unido na próxima semana. O premiê fará um discurso no Parlamento Europeu, em Estrasburgo, e participará da apresentação sobre o Estado da União Europeia feita pela presidente da Comissão Europeia, Ursula von der Leyen.

O jornal canadense The Globe and Mail informou, por sua vez, que foi a União Europeia, e não Carney, quem sugeriu o termo "membro associado". Citando uma fonte anônima, o veículo afirmou que ainda é cedo para discutir como essa relação poderia ser classificada.

Porta-vozes da Comissão Europeia não responderam aos pedidos de comentário.

A escalada da guerra comercial entre Canadá e Estados Unidos aumentou a pressão sobre Ottawa para fortalecer laços com outros parceiros comerciais.

As relações entre Ottawa e Washington se deterioraram desde o retorno de Donald Trump à Casa Branca, no ano passado, em meio a divergências sobre comércio e outros temas. A disputa resultou na imposição de tarifas sobre dezenas de bilhões de dólares em trocas comerciais entre os dois países.

Neste domingo, Trump voltou a criticar o Canadá, classificando o país como “o pior para negociar”, mas afirmou acreditar que os canadenses estejam “loucos para fechar um acordo”.

“Eles exploraram nosso país durante anos”, disse o presidente americano a jornalistas a bordo do Air Force One.

Trump também reafirmou a intenção de impor novas tarifas sobre carros, caminhões e autopeças do Canadá a partir de 1º de janeiro.

Segundo o Wall Street Journal, Canadá e União Europeia discutem formas de facilitar a circulação de bens, serviços e trabalhadores ligados a setores estratégicos, como energia, inteligência artificial, defesa e minerais críticos. Na prática, a medida aprofundaria a integração econômica entre os dois lados.

O jornal afirma ainda que as conversas incluem projetos para instalar cabos submarinos, construir centros de dados, ampliar sistemas de armazenamento em nuvem e desenvolver novas redes de satélite. Também estão em discussão investimentos em infraestrutura para exportar energia canadense para a Europa.

Carney também tem conversado regularmente com líderes europeus, especialmente o presidente francês Emmanuel Macron, sobre a possibilidade de permitir que canadenses vivam e trabalhem na União Europeia sem visto. A informação é do Wall Street Journal, que cita duas autoridades familiarizadas com o assunto.

Separadamente, a Presidência da França confirmou que Macron e Carney se encontrarão em 20 de setembro em Saint-Pierre e Miquelon, território francês próximo à costa atlântica do Canadá.

Qualquer iniciativa para aprofundar os laços entre Canadá e União Europeia, porém, deve enfrentar obstáculos. Experiências anteriores mostram que há resistência em partes da Europa até mesmo a acordos mais modestos.

Mais de uma década após ser firmado e nove anos depois de entrar em vigor de forma provisória, o acordo comercial entre Canadá e União Europeia ainda não foi ratificado por vários países do bloco.

articles.title: Edição genética promete revolucionar tratamento de doenças raras  | G1
articles.standfirst: As possibilidades vão desde tratar pacientes já nascidos até corrigir alterações genéticas ainda na fase embrionária. O uso da tecnologia, porém, divide especialistas e desperta debates éticos ao redor do mundo.
articles.summary: As possibilidades vão desde tratar pacientes já nascidos até corrigir alterações genéticas ainda na fase embrionária. O uso da tecnologia, porém, divide especialistas e desperta debates éticos ao redor do mundo.
articles.body:
A edição genética, antes restrita ao campo da ficção científica, está cada vez mais próxima da prática médica. Avanços recentes têm permitido corrigir alterações específicas no DNA humano para tratar doenças graves e raras, ao mesmo tempo em que reacendem debates sobre os limites éticos da manipulação genética. As possibilidades vão desde tratar pacientes já nascidos até modificar embriões antes mesmo do desenvolvimento de doenças hereditárias.

Um dos exemplos mais recentes é o caso de KJ, uma criança dos Estados Unidos que nasceu com uma doença genética rara que afeta o fígado e provoca o acúmulo de amônia no organismo. Logo após o nascimento, exames apontaram níveis da substância cerca de 100 vezes acima do normal, colocando sua vida em risco.

Após identificar duas mutações em um gene responsável pelo controle da amônia, médicos da Universidade da Pensilvânia desenvolveram um tratamento personalizado para o menino. A terapia utilizou uma técnica conhecida como CRISPR com edição de bases, capaz de alterar pontos específicos do DNA. O medicamento foi administrado por meio de infusões direcionadas ao fígado, órgão afetado pela doença.

Segundo os pesquisadores, o tratamento conseguiu melhorar significativamente o quadro clínico da criança. Hoje, aos dois anos, KJ apresenta desenvolvimento considerado normal para a idade, embora os médicos evitem falar em cura definitiva e ressaltem a necessidade de acompanhamento a longo prazo.

"A gente achava que ele não ia completar um ano": alteração de DNA permitiu tratamento de doença rara em bebê — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

O DNA humano contém cerca de 3 bilhões de letras químicas organizadas em aproximadamente 25 mil genes. Pequenas alterações nessa sequência podem ser suficientes para provocar doenças genéticas. A proposta da edição genética é corrigir esses erros diretamente na origem do problema.

A tecnologia CRISPR revolucionou esse campo ao permitir que cientistas identifiquem e modifiquem trechos específicos do material genético com precisão. Em alguns casos, basta corrigir uma única alteração para restaurar o funcionamento adequado de determinado gene.

Especialistas afirmam que os avanços atuais são consequência de décadas de pesquisas iniciadas com o Projeto Genoma Humano, lançado em 1990 para mapear toda a sequência do DNA humano. Desde a conclusão do projeto, em 2003, os exames genéticos ficaram mais rápidos e acessíveis, acelerando o desenvolvimento de novas terapias.

Apesar do potencial terapêutico, a edição genética também acumula episódios controversos. Em 2018, o biofísico chinês He Jiankui anunciou o nascimento de gêmeas que teriam tido o DNA modificado ainda na fase embrionária. O objetivo declarado era reduzir a vulnerabilidade futura ao HIV.

O anúncio provocou forte reação da comunidade científica internacional. Além dos questionamentos sobre segurança, especialistas criticaram o fato de os embriões não apresentarem doenças que justificassem a intervenção. Posteriormente, um tribunal chinês condenou o pesquisador a três anos de prisão.

O episódio transformou a edição genética de embriões em um dos temas mais delicados da ciência contemporânea e reforçou discussões sobre os riscos de mudanças hereditárias que podem ser transmitidas às próximas gerações.

O biofísico chinês He Jiankui anunciou o nascimento de gêmeas que teriam tido o DNA modificado ainda na fase embrionária — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Mesmo após a polêmica, estudos sobre edição genética de embriões não foram abandonados. Em junho deste ano, pesquisadores da Universidade Columbia, em Nova York, anunciaram testes bem-sucedidos de edição genética em embriões humanos. Entre os autores está o pesquisador e embriologista brasileiro Marcos Kuhlmann.

No experimento, os cientistas modificaram genes relacionados ao colesterol e à hemoglobina ainda na fase de zigoto, quando o embrião possui apenas uma célula. O objetivo era comprovar que a alteração genética podia ser feita com sucesso. Nenhum dos embriões foi implantado em um útero.

Os pesquisadores afirmam que a intenção futura é desenvolver tratamentos capazes de corrigir mutações genéticas antes do nascimento, evitando o surgimento de doenças hereditárias. Ao mesmo tempo, defendem que a tecnologia seja usada exclusivamente para fins de saúde, e não para a criação de características físicas ou biológicas sob encomenda.

Edição genética promete revolucionar tratamento de doenças raras — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Para especialistas, a edição genética representa uma das maiores transformações da medicina moderna, especialmente para pacientes com doenças raras. No entanto, a velocidade dos avanços científicos vem acompanhada da necessidade de estabelecer limites éticos claros sobre até onde a humanidade está disposta a modificar o próprio código genético.

Enquanto esse debate continua, histórias como a de KJ mostram o potencial da tecnologia para mudar vidas e oferecem esperança a famílias que convivem com doenças que, até pouco tempo atrás, não tinham tratamento disponível.

articles.title: Jharkhand businessman murder: How did traffic cop track victim’s phone? CP orders probe
articles.summary: Kolkata CP Ajay Nand orders internal probe after traffic sergeant’s arrest for allegedly sharing cell tower location and call records in Jharkhand murder case.
articles.body: KOLKATA: Kolkata Police commissioner Ajay Nand has ordered a high-level internal probe following the arrest of traffic police sergeant Ayan Gupta, a 2010-batch officer posted at the Beliaghata Traffic Guard, by Jharkhand Police in connection with the Aug 24 murder of a Jharkhand-based businessman.Gupta’s arrest revealed that he had allegedly supplied the accused with cell-tower locations and call records at the behest of Beliaghata Traffic Guard civic volunteer Twinkle Das, who allegedly maintained contact with the killers. A traffic sergeant in Kolkata Police is not authorised to access or provide such data.After the matter came to light, Nand ordered the internal probe. The local traffic guard has completed its preliminary inquiry and submitted its findings to Lalbazar. The police headquarters is now seeking to fix responsibility and ascertain whether anyone else was involved.Senior officers at Lalbazar said the top brass was closely monitoring the probe. Nand also confirmed to TOI via text message that the inquiry was underway, though he did not provide details.Investigators have learnt that Gupta allegedly supplied businessman Nikhil’s mobile tower location to Raghav, who is suspected to be the mastermind behind the murder. Twinkle, said to be a close associate of Raghav, has also been arrested.According to police sources, Gupta, a Parnasree resident, acted on requests from Twinkle, who lives in the Chaulpatti Road area. Gupta allegedly accessed Nikhil’s mobile tower location multiple times and passed the information to Raghav. Police suspect the location data was used to track Nikhil and plan his killing.Only authorised investigating officers in the Detective Department — including those attached to the Cyber Crime Branch or assigned to specific cases — and specialised technical units such as the Kolkata Police’s Special Task Force can officially seek and access mobile tower location data from telecom service providers, and only after obtaining the requisite legal permissions.“Ordinary citizens — and not even traffic police personnel — can directly request mobile tower logs or location-tracking data because of privacy and legal restrictions,” said a senior officer.Last Thursday, a Jharkhand Police team summoned Gupta and Twinkle to Lalbazar, where they were questioned at length by officers of the Detective Department. Sources said the entire interrogation was videographed. They were subsequently informed of their arrest.On Aug 24, businessman Nikhil was shot dead in front of a hotel along NH 33 in the Chandil police station area. Police said the attackers fired around nine rounds, hitting him in the shoulder, back and neck. He was taken in critical condition to a hospital in Jamshedpur, where doctors declared him dead.Although the case initially appeared to stem from business rivalry, the probe increasingly pointed to a contract killing.Police suspect the shooters were paid nearly Rs 15 lakh. articles.title: Incêndio destrói padaria e casa no bairro da terra firme, em Belém | G1
articles.standfirst: Incêndio iniciou na madrugada desta segunda-feira (14). Três pessoas conseguiram sair sem ferimentos, mas cinco animais da família morreram.
articles.summary: Incêndio iniciou na madrugada desta segunda-feira (14). Três pessoas conseguiram sair sem ferimentos, mas cinco animais da família morreram.
articles.body:
Um incêndio atingiu uma padaria e parte de uma residência no bairro da Terra Firme, em Belém .

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, três pessoas que estavam no imóvel conseguiram sair sem ferimentos. Cinco animais da família morreram: três cachorros, um gato e um papagaio.

De acordo com as informações preliminares, o fogo começou por volta das 2h, em uma área nos fundos da padaria usada como reservatório de lenha.

A parte da frente do estabelecimento não foi atingida, mas o incêndio se espalhou rapidamente para os fundos do imóvel.

A padaria e a casa pertencem ao mesmo proprietário. No terreno também funcionavam outros espaços. Todos esses ambientes foram atingidos pelas chamas.

A residência fica na parte superior do imóvel, de três andares. Segundo os bombeiros, moravam no local o dono da padaria, a mãe e a companheira. Nenhum deles ficou ferido.

Na manhã desta segunda-feira, os bombeiros permaneciam no local fazendo o trabalho de rescaldo para evitar novos focos de incêndio. As causas do sinistro ainda serão apuradas.

A denúncia foi apresentada pelo Ministério Público e aceita pela Justiça. O processo tramita em segredo de Justiça. A reportagem tenta localizar a defesa do réu.

Olga Beatriz morreu na primeira noite em que dormiu na casa do pai , no bairro Serra Dourada, em Várzea Grande , região metropolitana de Cuiabá. A informação foi confirmada ao g1 pela advogada da família, Dayanne Rodrigues.

Na época, o investigado afirmou à polícia que teria encontrado mensagens trocadas entre a filha e um garoto, o que teria motivado as agressões. A mãe da vítima contesta a versão apresentada por ele e afirma que a filha não tinha celular nem utilizava redes sociais .

Segundo a advogada, a mãe da adolescente estava separada de Claudinei após episódios de violência doméstica. Conforme o relato, Olga Beatriz insistia em manter contato com o pai e, por isso, a mãe permitia algumas visitas, mas sem que a filha passasse a noite na casa dele.

The device tested by Russian military organization GUGI could cut communications lines while leaving little physical evidence connecting Moscow to the incident.

The confrontation occurred near Svalbard, where two 1,400km cables connect the Arctic territory with mainland Norway beneath Arctic waters.

NATO disrupted Russia's Arctic cable exercise before the reported weapon could be deployed

Russian submarines rehearsed attacks that could leave little evidence afterward

Two 1,400km cables connect Svalbard with mainland Norway beneath Arctic waters

NATO allies disrupted a Russian naval exercise near Svalbard after detecting preparations involving a secret device intended for damaging subsea communications infrastructure.

British, Norwegian and American forces confronted vessels linked to Russia's deep-sea research directorate during exercises conducted in Arctic waters this spring.

The reported operation did not damage any cable, but officials said the equipment could remove evidence that would identify its use after an attack.

NATO confronted Russian vessels during Arctic cable exercise

The equipment was reportedly being tested by GUGI, a Russian military organization responsible for specialized underwater operations and deep-ocean missions.

Officials said the device could cut communications lines while leaving little physical evidence capable of connecting Moscow to the incident.

The confrontation occurred near Svalbard, where two fiber-optic cables extend for about 1,400km and descend roughly 2,700 meters underwater.

Those lines support data transfers from SvalSat, a major satellite ground facility that also serves NASA's Near Space Network in orbit.

The cables are only around garden-hose thickness, yet they support services carrying enormous quantities of information between the Arctic territory and Norway.

Norway is developing another connection involving Svalbard and Jan Mayen, with completion expected during 2028 under its current infrastructure plans.

The location matters militarily because vessels from Russia's northern naval facilities must cross the Bear Gap when entering Atlantic waters.

That passage spans roughly 400 miles, making nearby infrastructure significant for communications and surveillance across the wider High North region.

Why NATO is concerned about the cable-cutting capability

Western intelligence officials have become increasingly concerned that Moscow could expand covert disruption against critical infrastructure across Europe's vulnerable networks.

Three American officials told Reuters that subsea communications lines could feature in a future attempt to test NATO's collective-defense commitment.

CIA Director John Ratcliffe travelled to Moscow in August for discussions that included warnings about escalating sabotage activity in Europe.

Russia has rejected accusations that it conducts sabotage inside NATO countries or seeks direct military confrontation with the alliance, but Norway is not having it.

"Through our joint operation, we sent a clear message to Russia that they cannot operate covertly," Norway's Defense Minister Tore Sandvik declared in a statement.

"We have made it unequivocally clear to Russian authorities that any attempt to target our critical infrastructure will be detected and met with consequences."

Earlier British disclosures also linked Russian deep-sea submarines with activity near British waters involving energy pipelines and telecommunications systems.

Britain subsequently allocated another $136 million toward P-8 maritime patrol aircraft as suspicious Russian vessel movements increased around vulnerable infrastructure.

Undersea cables carry about 99% of Britain's international telecommunications and data traffic, raising concerns about disruptions to essential public services.

British and Norwegian officials have carried their findings to Moscow, apparently hoping public disclosure would discourage any future use of the technology.

However, reports so far do not establish that Russia has used this device against a cable, but rather that it has rehearsed its deployment.

The twist came later, when Wardogs developers acknowledged that the wrong player had been banned, turning a suspected cheating incident into an anti-cheat controversy.Summit1g gets banned during Wardogs streamThe incident unfolded while Summit1g was playing Wardogs, an FPS title that has been attracting attention from players and streamers. During the match, another player repeatedly took him out with what appeared to be suspicious one-shot sniper kills.Summit1g seemed convinced that something was wrong. Yet the situation took an unexpected turn when the streamer himself was suddenly disconnected.A notification first indicated that he had been logged out. Soon afterward, Summit1g received a permanent ban, with cheating given as the reason.His reaction captured the absurdity of the situation. Rather than becoming openly hostile, he questioned how the anti-cheat system could have reached that conclusion."I got banned? He was cheating. For real? You banned the wrong guy! You banned the wrong guy, man. I respect it, you know? We were almost there. It was close. No, no. Yeah, I really got to stretch now, man. Yo, man, no disrespect. It’s all good, dude. Mistakes happen. But it was the guy that was killing me. I sure as sh*t wasn’t killing him, you know? I was the victim."Summit1g then joked that his own performance may have contributed to the confusion. He suggested that the anti-cheat system could have interpreted his strong finish as evidence that something unusual was happening."I know it seemed like I was kicking, I was beating too much a*s at the end, though, bro. They may have seen me standing over like 20 bodies, and they were like, 'Dude, that guy is definitely cheating.'"The comments added a humorous edge to an otherwise serious problem. We always have to have a human involved. Well, this fg idiot here, when the human was involved, fg banned Summit instead of the cheater in Summit’s stream. So, f*****g good job."The explanation changes the story from a streamer simply being caught by an automated system to a much more unusual moderation error. It also highlights why human review can be both a safeguard and a potential source of mistakes.For Summit1g, the Wardogs incident became an unexpected reminder that even systems designed to catch cheaters can sometimes get the wrong player. articles.body: A day after President Trump expressed his support for Northern Ireland breaking from the UK to unify with the Republic of Ireland, the leaders of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland are gathering at a summit in Cardiff to sign a deal designed to kick-start the break-up of the United Kingdom.The three first ministers, all representing pro-independence parties thanks to Labour's disastrous performance at devolved elections in May, will call on British govt to "prepare, plan and facilitate constitutional change" in Wales, Scotland and the north of Ireland.Leader of the Scottish National Party John Swinney, Leader of Plaid Cymru Rhun ap Iorwerth, Sinn Fein President Mary Lou McDonald and Sinn Fein Vice-President Michelle O'Neill issued a statement Sunday to say they are meeting in Cardiff to "strengthen the cooperation of Wales, Scotland and Ireland" and build towards constitutional change.When Trump said a "unified Ireland is going to happen eventually," he might have known something UK PM Andy Burnham didn't. At Prime Minister's Questions last week Burnham made the strange comment that both in Scotland and Northern Ireland a border poll would be considered if there was a clear consensus that public opinion had changed - even though this is only the case for Northern Ireland. Scotland has no equivalent statutory trigger. He was then forced to write a letter to Swinney saying that independence and a referendum in Scotland "are off limits". "Burnham doesn't seem to know the basics of the UK Government's position on the Union," a source close to Swinney told the Sunday Telegraph.Swinney said on Sunday: "We are at a pivotal moment of constitutional change, and our parties share the common belief that our interests will never be served by Westminster, and that the people of our respective nations must have a meaningful say over their future."Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: A railway at a UK nuclear waste site has gained an unusual new feature: sleepers made largely from recycled plastic. In 2025, the Low Level Waste Repository began installing composite sleepers as part of routine maintenance on its rail sidings, replacing traditional hardwood with a material designed to last for decades. According to Nuclear Waste Services, each sleeper contains approximately 90kg of recycled plastic waste, while the organisation says the products can remain in service for between 50 and 100 years. Made in the UK and fully recyclable, the sleepers mark a small but notable change in how the Repository is maintaining its railway infrastructure.Each railway sleeper uses 90kg of recycled plasticThe most striking part of the change is the amount of recycled material contained in each sleeper. Nuclear Waste Services said the composite sleepers are made from approximately 90kg of recycled plastic waste, giving material that might otherwise have been discarded another use within a working railway system.The organisation also stated that the sleepers have a claimed lifespan of between 50 and 100 years. According to the May 2025 edition of the NWS newsletter, they are made in the UK and are fully recyclable. This combination of recycled content, long stated service life and recyclability was part of the reason they were selected as an alternative to traditional hardwood sleepers.Recycled-plastic sleepers were installed during routine maintenanceThe switch was not described as a full replacement programme from the outset. Nuclear Waste Services said it had installed the recycled-plastic composite sleepers as part of the maintenance work and planned to transition fully to composite sleepers as required. The Repository therefore became the first site in the Nuclear Decommissioning Authority group to install these particular sleepers.That distinction is significant because the project was not simply about replacing worn railway components. The source describes the work as an effort to improve sustainability while maintaining an important piece of site infrastructure. The rail sidings support operations at the Repository, making the sleepers a relatively small component of a much larger nuclear waste management site.Ruth Davey welcomes the move to more sustainable railway sleepersRuth Davey, Senior Environmental Advisor at Nuclear Waste Services, welcomed the change, describing it as an example of the organisation's values being put into practice. She said the replacement showed the Repository Engineering team being “action-oriented” in securing more sustainable materials for a key asset at the site, with benefits considered both financially and environmentally.The project illustrates how sustainability measures can be introduced through ordinary maintenance rather than requiring an entirely separate infrastructure project. What it does establish is that the new sleepers use approximately 90kg of recycled plastic each, are claimed to last 50 to 100 years, are fully recyclable and have begun replacing traditional hardwood sleepers at the UK nuclear waste site.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Gujarat to global: How idea to fix pollution has lessons for Delhi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Nearly 15 years ago, a handful of economists, engineers and regulators began wrestling with a question in Gujarat. Could factories be persu.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Nearly 15 years ago, a handful of economists, engineers and regulators began wrestling with a question in Gujarat. Could factories be persuaded to cut pollution without fearing a shutdown?Today, that experiment has an answer in the emissions trading scheme (ETS), which is travelling nearly 14,000 km from India, poised to become one of the country’s newest environmental exports.After transforming industrial pollution regulations in Gujarat and inspiring similar programmes in Maharashtra and Rajasthan, the idea that germinated in India is headed to Rio de Janeiro.The Brazilian city has signed a letter of intent to examine adapting this approach to its own pollution challenges.If implemented, Rio would become South America’s first emissions trading system for industrial partic­ulate pollution.For Delhi-NCR, which is annually in the news for its winter air pollution crisis, the Gujarat experience also offers a useful model, which is centred around incentives that make industries compete to pollute less, rather than punishing them when they pollute more.For decades, India’s industrial pollution control has relied largely on periodic inspections and shutdown notices when factories breached emission limits. Researchers believed there was a better way — one that rewarded environmentally cleaner factories, instead of treating every factory in the same way.The idea is simple. Regulators set a maximum pollution limit for an industrial cluster and divide it into permits.Factories that cut emissions beyond their target can sell surplus permits to plants finding it harder or costlier to clean up. Cleaner factories can earn, while others get flexibility to comply. At the same time, the pollution stays within the overall cap.The approach was piloted in Surat in 2019 by researchers affiliated with the Energy Policy Institute at the University of Chicago (EPIC) and J-PAL, which was working with Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB).The pilot covered 162 of Gujarat’s 317 large coal-burning industrial plants, while the rest remained under conventional regulation, allowing researchers to compare the two approaches.In the randomised trial, the participating plants cut particulate emissions by 20-30% and pollution-control costs by 11%. Compliance touched 99%, against roughly two-thirds under the conventional system.Researchers estimated the benefits exceeded costs by at least 25 times.Conventionally, a typical plant emitted around 1,300 kg of particulate matter a month.Emissions from similar industries operating under the ETS fell to roughly 900-1,000 kg a month — a 20-30% reduction that held across all 10 compliance periods during the nearly two-year study from April 2019 to 2021.The flexibility built into the system allowed firms to meet their pollution commitments more efficiently and at a lower cost. “This pollution market was made in India, tested in India and it succeeded in India.Just as pollution doesn’t respect borders, ideas don’t respect borders too,” said Emissions Market Accelerator (EMA) co-chair Michael Greenstone, one of the four researchers who worked with GPCB on the experiment.For Dr Kaushik Deb, the executive director of EMA, the challenge lay in convincing industrial units that cleaner air need not come at the expense of growth.“The first reaction was, ‘why another form of regulation?’ But we created the scheme such that there were no losers,” Deb told TOI. Only one industrial closure occurred under the system in seven years, he said.Today, the programme covers a population of nearly 300 million across the country and is expanding to sulphur dioxide and wastew-ater pollution.Dr Bala Srinivasan, the EMA co-chair, said the international journey accelerated after Gujarat became an Earthshot Prize Finalist in 2025. Founded by Prince William, the prize identifies and helps scale breakthrough environmental solutions from thousands of entries worldwide.“Earthshot suddenly gave us a lot of global exposure,” Srinivasan said. That visibility, he said, helped open conversations beyond India — including Rio — and generated fresh interest among Indian states as the prize prepares to come to Mumbai later this year.For Delhi-NCR, the Gujarat experiment offers a different way of thinking about industrial pollution, and gives industries an economic reason to reduce emissions, rather than relying only on inspections, penalties and shutdowns.While the pollution problem of the national capital region is far more complex than Surat’s industrial cluster, and the Gujarat model cannot simply be transplanted, the experts suggest that less emission across sectors can become a competitive advantage rather than merely a regulatory burden.In a region where repeated restrictions have often produced friction between pollution control and economic activity, that may be a lesson worth examining.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.body: In a cramped workshop near the front line in north-eastern Ukraine, military mechanic "Chimera" is helping prepare his unit's robot forces for battle. Lined up in a row, the four-wheeled unmanned vehicles known as "Hyenas" will crawl toward Russian lines with their payload of explosives and attack an enemy dugout or halt an advance.Similar models have captured Russian prisoners, said Chimera (44), who asked to be identified by his call sign. "Imagine what 20 kilograms of explosives is like: it's very powerful," he said. "Very powerful." Workshops like this one, run by Ukraine's Third Army Corps, have sprouted up across the 1,200-km front as Kyiv's outmanned army seeks to gain the technological edge against Russia's unrelenting infantry assaults in the fifth year of war.Unmanned ground vehicles are a critical new component of Ukraine's strategy to fight smarter by preserving the lives of its troops on a drone-saturated battlefield, where virtually any movement can prove deadly. Most Ukrainian brigades feature unmanned systems units which are expanding to include UGVs as part of their forces.New 'revolution'In the workshop, a garage space is crammed with experimental drones, some with tracks and others wheeled. One is mounted with a hose for dousing fires; another is equipped with a rack to hold portable rocket launchers. Brigadier General Andrii Biletskyi, who commands the Third Army Corps, described the gradual replacement of infantrymen with UGVs as the next "revolution" in warfare.Considered one of Ukraine's premier forces, the corps wants to replace around one-third of its frontline troops by the end of the year. "The West slept through the (drone) revolution in many ways," he said, adding the infantry now performs just 10% of the tasks it did before the constant aerial threat appeared. "If the West really wants to not just keep up with the times, but to get ahead, it needs to think about the next revolution," said Biletskyi.Inside a grey command centre in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, the ground drone operators of NC13, formed last year, are manifesting Biletskyi's vision in real time, controllers in hand. Deputy commander "Bar" said his unit runs operations virtually every day. In one, they loaded three bombs onto a trailer that was pulled onto a bridge used for enemy logistics, then blown up. In another, a machine-gun-mounted UGV suppressed an enemy assault while kamikaze drones rained on them from above.Room for creationThough not a miracle weapon, ground drones are one more step toward the automation of warfare, said Biletskyi. They could shape new frontline tactics, with commanders more open to daring operations that would have otherwise led to heavy losses. "War is a creative activity; it's an art," he said. "Otherwise, a commander is not called a commander - but a butcher." ReutersCatch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Trump eyes Iran oil, hints at Venezuela-style US control after war
articles.summary: US News: US President Donald Trump on Sunday suggested that the United States could remain in Iran after the war and take control of its oil resources, drawing.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Sunday suggested that the United States could remain in Iran after the war and take control of its oil resources, drawing a comparison with Washington's post-Maduro role in Venezuela.Speaking at the Irish open golf championship during his visit to Ireland, Trump said the US would ultimately leave Iran unless it decided to stay and "keep the oil like Venezuela". He also said he expected the war to end "right after the midterms, maybe before", referring to the US elections in November.Trump said Iran was "calling constantly" to seek a deal, but insisted Washington would accept only an agreement that met its demands. "We have to make the right deal," he said, adding that he would not accept a deal that was "not a good deal".His comments came as the conflict continued to disrupt energy markets. Oil prices have risen above $100 a barrel, while US diesel prices hit a record above $6.20 a gallon. Trump said that once the war ends, US gasoline prices would "drop like a rock".Trump's reference to Venezuela follows the US military operation that captured Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro on January 3. Reuters reported that the operation was planned for months and involved extensive rehearsals by US Special Forces, including using a mock-up of Maduro's safe house. CIA personnel also provided intelligence on his movements.US forces captured Maduro and his wife in Caracas before taking him to the United States to face criminal charges. The operation followed months of pressure by the Trump administration.Washington subsequently moved to take a major role in Venezuela's oil sector, including controlling oil sales and pursuing arrangements giving US interests access to the country's vast crude reserves.Trump's remarks now raise the prospect of applying a similar economic model to Iran, linking a possible long-term US presence there not only to security objectives but also to access to its oil wealth.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Russia targeting EU, UK officials? Ukraine’s big claim after drone strike
articles.summary: Europe News: A Russian drone strike on a train near the Ukraine-Poland border may have been aimed at a diplomatic train carrying former UK Prime Minister Boris Joh.
articles.body: A Russian drone strike on a train near the Ukraine-Poland border may have been aimed at a diplomatic train carrying former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson, former Swedish Prime Minister Carl Bildt and European security officials, Ukraine’s state railway operator has claimed.The drone struck a locomotive at Yahodyn station, around 2 km from the Polish border, shortly after the diplomatic train carrying the senior officials had passed through the area. No casualties were reported.According to Ukrzaliznytsia, the diplomatic train had left the station earlier than scheduled after railway authorities adjusted timetables in real time because of the continuing threat of Russian strikes.“It is quite likely that the target of this Russian drone could also have been the diplomatic train,” the railway operator said, according to the Daily Mail.Ukrzaliznytsia later confirmed that the diplomatic train had been at the site shortly before the strike. It said the train was carrying security advisers from several European Union member states, along with former European leaders including Johnson.The delegation had been returning from the Yalta European Strategy conference in Kyiv. Bildt later shared footage of the attack on X, saying the train struck was not theirs but had been travelling just minutes behind them.“This wasn't our train, but the one just minutes after us by the Polish border crossing,” Bildt said. “It was evacuated as the Russian drone approached and no one was hurt.”Another train carrying former CIA Director David Petraeus was reportedly still at Yahodyn station when the drone struck.Johnson condemned the attack, describing it as “random and senseless” and saying it reflected the kind of attacks Ukrainians face on a daily basis.The incident has raised concerns over the safety of foreign officials travelling through western Ukraine, particularly as the strike occurred close to the border of NATO member Poland.Russia has not said that the diplomatic train was the intended target. Moscow said its forces had targeted infrastructure facilitating the movement of military cargo from Europe into western Ukraine.The strike came amid a broader escalation in long-range attacks. Earlier on Sunday, a Russian drone also hit a truck near the Ukraine-Poland border, temporarily disrupting operations at the Yahodyn-Dorohusk crossing.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Indian-origin CEO spent ₹3.5 crore on his girlfriend, then sought it back after their breakup: What followed is an unusual court battle
articles.summary: A relationship that began with flights, luxury gifts and lavish spending eventually found its way into a Singapore courtroom after an Indian-origin bu.
articles.body: A relationship that began with flights, luxury gifts and lavish spending eventually found its way into a Singapore courtroom after an Indian-origin businessman sought to recover nearly ₹3.5 crore he said he had spent on his former girlfriend.Chander Agarwal, CEO and managing director of logistics company TCI Express, had told the Singapore High Court that the money he spent on Felicia Lee during their relationship was not simply a series of gifts. He claimed the payments were interest-free loans that she was supposed to repay.Lee disagreed. Her position was that the money and expensive purchases had been given to her out of love and affection, with no expectation of repayment.The case has attracted attention because of its unusual nature of dispute. But what did the court say and who did it ultimately side with? Here’s the full story.They met on a flight in 2019Agarwal and the woman, Felicia Lee, met on a flight in 2019, as per the court hearing, published in Laws.sg. He later contacted her on social media and the two began meeting. Their relationship became romantic in September 2022.But Agarwal's spending on Lee had started even before they officially became a couple. The judgment records a long list of gifts and experiences Agarwal had paid for, including luxury shopping, first-class or suites-class flights, international travel and expensive dinners.Among the gifts mentioned were a Louis Vuitton handbag, Prada vouchers and an Apple Hermès watch. He also paid for a Europe trip covering destinations including Barcelona, Lisbon and London, along with accommodation and luxury purchases.Then the relationship endedThe relationship came to an end in December 2023 after Agarwal suspected Lee of being unfaithful. What had once been spending between two people in a relationship soon acquired a very different meaning. In March 2024, Agarwal filed a lawsuit seeking to recover various amounts he said he had spent on Lee. The total claim was about SGD 468,090- which is more than ₹3.5 crore.His argument was that the money was not simply given away. He claimed the sums were interest-free loans and that Lee was required to repay them. Lee disputed that account.Her position was essentially that the money had been spent on her as gifts during their relationship and that there had been no agreement requiring her to return it.The unusual question before the courtThe case therefore turned less on whether Agarwal had actually spent the money and more on why he had spent it. There was evidence of the substantial sums involved, but the court had to determine whether those payments were loans or gifts.During cross-examination, Agarwal reportedly said that once they began dating, "everything became a loan, everything was transactional", while spending before the relationship had not been treated that way.He also argued that once Lee accepted his offers to spend his money, those expenses could effectively become loans. That distinction became crucial to the case.What the Singapore court saidThe Singapore High Court eventually rejected Agarwal's claim, finding that most of the disputed money had been given as gifts rather than loans.In its September 9 judgment, the court noted that Agarwal had willingly spent large amounts on Lee during their relationship and that the evidence did not support his claim that the money was meant to be repaid.The judge also found it difficult to accept the argument that simply accepting someone's offer to spend money could automatically turn that spending into a loan.According to Moneycontrol, Senior Judge Lee Seiu Kin described the evidence as showing that Agarwal had "showered her with expensive gifts" during the relationship.The judge further observed that the dispute appeared to have taken a different turn after the relationship ended, saying that Agarwal had become determined to recover a price from Lee after the relationship ended badly.The court ultimately ruled that the payments in question were gifts and dismissed his attempt to recover the money. Agarwal was also ordered to pay Lee's legal costs.For a relationship that began with a chance meeting on a flight and unfolded through luxury trips, designer purchases and generous spending, its final chapter ended not over a romantic gesture, but over a very different question- whether those gestures were ever meant to be paid back.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: China scales back troops along LAC amid thaw in ties with India; down to 10 Arms Brigade
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: China has significantly reduced the deployment of its People’s Liberation Army (PLA) forces along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in 2025,.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: China has significantly reduced the deployment of its People’s Liberation Army (PLA) forces along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in 2025, the ministry of defence said in a statement.The ministry said the year witnessed a “significant reduction in deployment” of PLA forces opposite India’s northern borders. It said 10 Combined Arms Brigade-size forces remained deployed in areas along the LAC and in traditional training areas.At the same time, the Indian Army’s deployment across all sectors of the LAC remained “robust, well poised and prepared to deal with any emerging contingency”, the ministry said.The reduction in Chinese troop deployment came amid increased political, diplomatic and military engagement between India and China, which the ministry said helped bring greater stability along the Northern Borders.India and China resumed several mechanisms for dialogue during the year. The 33rd and 34th rounds of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) were held in March and July 2025 respectively. Special Representatives’ talks on the boundary question also resumed, with rounds held in December 2024 and August 2025.The ministry said the improvement in bilateral ties was further reinforced by PM Modi’s visit to China for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Tianjin in August 2025. Military-level engagement also continued, including the 23rd Corps Commander Level Meet in Eastern Ladakh on October 25-26, 2025.“Border Personnel Meetings continue with the PLA in all sectors in a cordial and friendly environment to resolve issues of concern,” the ministry said.The latest developments come as India-China ties continue to show signs of stabilisation following years of tensions along the disputed border.PM Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping held a bilateral meeting lasting more than 50 minutes in New Delhi on Saturday, on the sidelines of the Brics Summit. Welcoming Xi, PM Modi said the two countries now had an opportunity to discuss bilateral cooperation.Xi said China viewed India-China relations from a “strategic and long-term perspective” and called for both countries to work together on shared development.“In the face of a complex international landscape marked by intertwined changes and challenges, China and India, as the world's two most populous countries and important members of the Global South, shoulder significant responsibilities,” Xi said.

articles.title: 'Everyone's been bugging me': Trump to remove 10% duty on Irish whiskey
articles.summary: US News: US President Donald Trump attended the Irish Open in Ireland on Sunday and announced plans to remove the United States’ 10% tariff on Irish whiskey, s.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump attended the Irish Open in Ireland on Sunday and announced plans to remove the United States’ 10% tariff on Irish whiskey, saying he had faced repeated calls to drop the duty from Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin, golfers and others.Trump made the announcement during the trophy ceremony after Irish golfer Shane Lowry won the tournament. The surprise move drew loud whistles and cheers from spectators, although it was not immediately clear when the tariff would be lifted."Everybody's been bugging me" to do it, Trump said. "And I said, on behalf of the United States of America, I am going to take the tariffs off" of Irish whiskey.Trump said Martin and several golfers had raised the issue with him, with Lowry among those who asked him to reconsider the tariff.Irish whiskey currently faces the standard tariff imposed by the Trump administration on most imports from the European Union. The rate was reduced from 15% to 10% in July.The planned move would also address an imbalance created after Trump announced in April that certain tariffs on whiskey from the United Kingdom would be lifted. The concession covers Scotch and spirits made in Northern Ireland, leaving Irish whiskey subject to a higher trade barrier.Chris Swonger, president and CEO of the Distilled Spirits Council of the United States, welcomed Trump's announcement, calling it "another positive step toward reducing barriers to spirits trade".He said the move would benefit businesses and consumers during the upcoming holiday season."As US hospitality businesses enter the critical holiday season, this action will provide a welcome boost for retailers, restaurants, consumers and the American economy," Swonger said.The Irish Whiskey Association had called for the tariff to be removed in May. It said doing so would help US companies that sell Irish products and reduce uncertainty for consumers.Trump had previously linked the UK tariff concession to a visit by King Charles III and Queen Camilla to the White House on April 30."The King and Queen got me to do something that nobody else was able to do, without hardly even asking!" Trump posted on social media at the time.The Scotch Whisky Association said on July 24 that the zero-tariff arrangement for Scotch had come into effect.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
